subject: HEUR-042 and answer-balance-audit count ties and trivial gaps as exploitable, burying the real offenders
description: Found 2026-09-27 while clearing NP-17. Both the EduScan rule and the audit report correct-is-longest as a COUNT, which conflates cases that differ by two orders of magnitude in exploitability. Concrete: dns-dhcp Q3 is flagged because AAAA (4 chars) is longer than A, MX and NS - unexploitable - and counted identically to Q8 where the correct answer is 98 chars against distractors of 22 to 49. Of 73 flagged questions across the 7 Network+ quizzes, only 48 were material by a gap-plus-prose-length test; the other 25 were acronyms and near-ties. The reverse also bites: troubleshooting's count did not move at all (53.3% before and after) while its real gaps collapsed from +35/+53/+35 to +5/+15/+2, so the count understated completed work and overstated remaining risk simultaneously. PLATFORM IMPACT: the audit calls 244 quizzes exploitable today, and that list almost certainly mixes 100%-longest-with-+50-gaps files in with tie-heavy ones where every option is the same shape by construction (channel lists like '1, 6, 11' vs '2, 7, 12' can never be balanced by length). Someone working that backlog cannot tell which is which. FIX: report and sort by GAP (max-other-option minus correct) alongside the count, and exclude or separately bucket questions whose options are all short tokens. A second, smaller inconsistency found the same day: _tools/eduscan/answer-length-detail.js counts ties as longest while answer-balance-audit.js does not, so the two tools disagree on the same file by exactly the tie count - they should share one definition.
